articleTitle: Clinical outcomes of quadriceps, hamstring, and bone-patellar tendon-bone autografts for ACL reconstruction: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
takeaways: This meta-analysis examined only the study protocol and objectives for comparing quadriceps tendon, hamstring tendon, and bone-patellar tendon-bone autografts in ACL reconstruction, but the actual results and findings are not yet available in the provided abstract

The study specifically focused on analyzing randomized controlled trials to compare donor-site morbidity, long-term graft survival, knee stability, and complication rates between the three autograft types
High-level evidence from randomized controlled trials directly comparing quadriceps tendon grafts with hamstring or bone-patellar tendon-bone grafts remains limited according to the researchers
The quadriceps tendon has emerged as a reliable autograft option for ACL reconstruction, though key comparative data on outcomes versus other graft types still needs clarification
